Definition: probably to shake out, i.e. (by implication) to scatter profusely; figuratively, to treat lightly
BiblicalUsage: Zuwl means to pour out lavishly — or, turned the other way, to despise. Isaiah pictures men lavishing gold from the bag to make a god, pouring out wealth on an idol; Lamentations pictures Jerusalem despised, her nakedness seen, because she sinned grievously. Lavish on an idol, or despised for sin: the word holds both.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that what we lavish our gold on shows what we worship, and that Jerusalem's shame is what happens when the worship goes wrong.
